What is your favorite life pro tip?

Work hard and follow your passion. This means you need to be practicing that thing that you love and doing it everyday. You got to learn to say "No" to people, especially the people who want you to drop your passion to just have fun. Also learning how to ignore that voice inside you that tells you you're not good enough. Just keep working hard and don't give up. You'll get to where you want to be :)

"There's no need to muddy the waters here boy." Spoken to a young me by an auto insurance salesman after I explained that there were several tickets written to me that should be on my DMV record, but weren't. In all things just Keep It Simple Stupid. Very few people like puzzling their way around through a complicated scenario.

I'd have to say that my favorite one is to never make assumptions unless you have a reasonable amount of evidence to base it off of. I can give you an example in any retail job: rude or frustrated customers not having it with anything. Sometimes the only difference between that really chill customer and the mean one is just a really crappy day or a big, emotional event that happened to them recently.

My favorite online writing piece on this very subject is one from the TalesFromTechSupport sub on Reddit: "Don't bother sending a tech, I'll be dead by then".

Though, one might ask how this 'tip' is beneficial and I understand where they're coming from. Yeah, sure, the only real effect is how easy it is to keep your cool in those types of situations when you adopt this thought process, but one possible outcome is how easy it is to change the attitudes of some of those mean people in the course of a small forty-five second conversation. I think eliminating a few mean people from your day's experience is worth it.

That's a good tip.
